issues.problem: The brief says to read the Oct 10 Brown crowd first. Oct 10 is today and the Oct 20 opener is ten days out. No order or ProShop allocation can react to a preseason crowd, so the gate cannot work.
issues.fix: Lock the October assortment now on a no-Brown rule. Use Oct 10 only as a social listen that shapes the Jan 21 plan. Say plainly that the Jan 21 call is made in December, not on the night.

issues.problem: The brief labels the City Edition a 2027-28 pitch, which is honest. But the 2026-27 City Edition is unverified and Specter's Celtics design and wear dates are unknown. Several avoid-rules (no gold, no repeats) are written against sets nobody has seen.
issues.fix: Keep the 2027-28 label at the top of the concept. Add one line saying the avoid list must be re-checked against the 2026-27 City Edition and Specter once both are public.

issues.problem: Specter and its merchandise went on sale Sept 9. A heritage launch on Oct 23 is not a launch of anything new, and the Oct 20 opener at Detroit on NBC is skipped as a retail moment. The Oct 30 Hawks Cup Night tee has only a week of lead after the Knicks game.
issues.fix: Call Oct 23 a restock and push of green heritage next to Specter already on shelves. Put a Tatum jersey and tee presence on the ProShop floor for the Oct 20 broadcast. Approve the Cup Night tee art before Oct 23.

issues.target: topInsights[0] and opportunities[0] (Tatum as the only deep player line)
issues.problem: The roster has changed more than the brief admits. Paul George, Mitchell Robinson, Mike Conley and Queta's new $56M extension are new faces. Derrick White is a Boston-favorite name that the product plan never touches. Betting only on Tatum puts the whole player line behind one man whose father just ripped the roster in public.
issues.fix: Add a small player tier: a Queta piece, since the brief already has his Cambridge court story, and a White piece if his status holds. Keep George off product until fans show they want him.

issues.problem: The Most call is the strongest local sound in the brief, but it is a licensed broadcast and a quoted line. Releasing it on Jan 21, the night Brown returns, also risks reading as a shot at Brown. The brief says the night is about the rivalry, yet the Sixers rivalry is where Brown now plays.
issues.fix: Describe the call in graphics and numbers, not quoted text. Clear it with the Celtics and the Most estate before design lock. Move the tee to a week earlier or later than Jan 21 and keep Jan 21 product silent.

issues.target: uniform.palette (green, white, granite, Beacon Hill violet)
issues.problem: Violet is the sharpest local idea in the brief, but it is a detail only locals will spot. Granite gray and white on a green base is close to any green team's set. The brief itself says to keep fronts clean and green, so the Boston story is almost invisible on court.
issues.fix: Make the neighborhood name list on the side panel the first thing a viewer sees, and keep violet as the hidden neck tape. Test the concept without the color notes and see if it still reads as Boston.

issues.problem: The plan is respectful and names paid co-authors, but a Black History Month collection from Nike built on Russell's story needs more than a launch location. The Russell estate, the Museum of African American History and the artists are all named, yet no one has said yes, and the Celtics' February game date is unknown.
issues.fix: Sign the artists and the estate before the collection is announced. Give the artists approval over the Russell 11 graphic. If the estate declines, drop Russell by name and keep the Chuck Cooper and 1964 starting-five story.

issues.problem: The whole neighborhood capsule rests on two small makers, Mathmatik Athletics and Madrugada. The brief admits neither has a confirmed 2026 trading status. A June launch with pre-orders in May needs signed deals by winter, and a small brand cannot absorb a Nike-sized run.
issues.fix: Verify both brands this month. Cap the first run and pay up front. Name two backup makers per neighborhood, one each in Mattapan and East Boston, where the brief names none.

issues.problem: An Aran-knit pack, a dockworker tattoo tee and a Dropkick Murphys pitch stack Irish cues in one March week. Even with no leprechauns, that is close to the Irish kitsch the uniform avoid list rules out. Evacuation Day is a South Boston holiday with real local meaning, not a theme.
issues.fix: Cut the pack to the Aran beanie and sweater. Treat the Murphys as a credited, paid creative partner or drop them. Pull the dockworker tee until a South Boston maker designs it.

issues.problem: The Portuguese green-and-red accents are a careful idea, but Queta is of Guinea-Bissau heritage and was raised in Portugal. Using Portuguese bakeries and artists as the story partners can read as covering the wrong community. The brief also plans it for September, a month the brief already crowds with Allston move-in.
issues.fix: Ask Queta's camp first which community he wants credited. Move the capsule to a quieter date, or tie it to the contract extension news now.

issues.problem: A coffee-colored sneaker with an ice-cube outsole is a clever idea, but the brief says to use no Dunkin' marks and still sells a Dunkin' ritual. The nearest read is a Dunkin' Dunk, which Nike has done before. Boston Concepts fans may see it as a repeat of the lobster joke.
issues.fix: Show the idea to Concepts with two alternates before committing. Make the tan and cream palette work without the coffee reference.

issues.target: topInsights[2] and risks[2] (New Balance, adidas, Converse)
issues.problem: The brief names the rival-brand map well, but it ignores a stronger use of it: Nike product is worn on court by Tatum and the whole team, and no piece says so. The Converse dynasty-era link is a risk note, not a product idea.
issues.fix: Add a Tatum-and-team-court tee that names the Garden floor. If Converse status is confirmed, pitch one dynasty-era throwback with Converse's blessing.

issues.target: calendar[0] (Fort Point Open Studios, Head of the Charles)
issues.problem: The play reads 'Scout commission artists', which is a stray line from the workflow and not a plan. Oct 16-18 is also four days from today, too late to commission artists and print tees.
issues.fix: Rewrite as 'Commission Fort Point artists for the 2027 Open Studios'. Use this year's weekend only to meet artists and pick partners.

issues.problem: A culture score of 84 and a fandom score of 82 are high for a fan base the brief itself calls unsettled, with a heat of 64. The rationale does not explain why a Brown trade and a possible 3-1 hangover leave fandom this strong.
issues.fix: Lower fandom by a few points, or say in the rationale that loyalty to the banners is what holds the score up.

strengths: The core thesis is right for Boston: fans trust the banners, the green and the parquet before any player. That holds whether Tatum thrives or not.
The rival-brand map is honest. It admits that New Balance, adidas and Converse own parts of the city and routes Nike through Concepts, Tatum and Garden nights.
The nor'easter line under the $175 tax line is a specific, local retail idea. It would not work in another city.
Neighborhood and Black-history ideas name paid co-authors, pay them, and keep launches in Nubian Square and Dot Ave and not at the Garden.
The uniform concept is labeled a 2027-28 pitch, and the brief flags what it cannot confirm, such as Specter wear dates and open doors.
summary: A strong, honest brief with a right-sized thesis and good local detail. Its weak points are timing and dependence. The Oct 10 gate cannot work. Several launches rest on unverified partners or an unseen City Edition and Specter. The player line leans on Tatum alone after a big roster change. Fix those, soften the March Irish cluster, and the plan holds up.
